envelope.basis: One envelope of Fleischmann's active dry yeast is 1/4 oz (7 g), 2 1/4 teaspoons

package.basis: One envelope of Fleischmann's active dry yeast is 1/4 oz (7 g), 2 1/4 teaspoons

packet.basis: One envelope of Fleischmann's active dry yeast is 1/4 oz (7 g), 2 1/4 teaspoons

bunch.basis: '2 pounds thin asparagus spears (2 bunches)', so a bunch is about 1 pound as bought (America's Test Kitchen, Simple Broiled Asparagus)

can.basis: Standard US can of broth: 14.5 oz (411 g), as for Swanson chicken broth
Standard US can of beans: 15 oz (425 g) (Bush's Black Beans, 15 oz can)

blood orange.basis: USDA SR Legacy 169098 (Orange juice, raw): juice of 1 orange ("1 fruit yields") = 86 g; a blood orange is an orange variety
1 orange yields 1 to 1 1/2 tbsp zest (Baking Bites), taken as 1 1/4 tbsp; USDA SR Legacy orange peel is 96 g per cup, so 6 g per tbsp; a blood orange is an orange variety

head large.basis: '1 large head broccoli (about 1 3/4 pounds)' (America's Test Kitchen, Roasted Broccoli)

head medium.basis: A typical medium head of broccoli is about 9 ounces (howmuchisin.com)

can.basis: Standard US can of corn kernels: 15.25 oz (432 g) net (Del Monte Whole Kernel Corn). The catalog's canned corn is drained solids, so using the net weight slightly overstates a can
Standard US can of beans: 15 oz (425 g), as for black beans; some cannellini cans are 15.5 oz
Standard US can of broth: 14.5 oz (411 g) (Swanson Chicken Broth, 14.5 oz can)
Standard US can of chickpeas: 15.5 oz (439 g) (Goya Chick Peas, 15.5 oz can)
Standard US can of chipotles in adobo: 7 oz (198 g) (La Costeña)

bunch.basis: A bunch of cilantro weighs about 2.8 ounces (79 g) (howmuchisin.com, measured at grocery stores); America's Test Kitchen uses 3-ounce packages

can.basis: Standard US can of coconut milk: 13.66 fl oz (404 ml) (Thai Kitchen), times USDA's density for canned coconut milk (226 g/cup, 0.955 g/ml)
Standard US can of diced green chiles: 4 oz (113 g) (Ortega)
Standard small US can of tomatoes: 14.5 oz (411 g) (Hunt's Diced Tomatoes, 14.5 oz can)
Standard US can of evaporated milk: 12 fl oz (354 ml) (Carnation), times USDA's density for evaporated milk (252 g/cup, 1.065 g/ml)

1 inch piece.basis: A 1-inch piece of ginger about 1 inch across weighs about 0.26 oz (7.4 g) (howmuchisin.com produce converter)

1/2 inch piece.basis: Half of a 1-inch piece: A 1-inch piece of ginger about 1 inch across weighs about 0.26 oz (7.4 g) (howmuchisin.com produce converter)

2 inch piece.basis: Twice a 1-inch piece: A 1-inch piece of ginger about 1 inch across weighs about 0.26 oz (7.4 g) (howmuchisin.com produce converter)

3 inch piece.basis: Three times a 1-inch piece: A 1-inch piece of ginger about 1 inch across weighs about 0.26 oz (7.4 g) (howmuchisin.com produce converter)

grapefruit.basis: USDA SR Legacy 173039 (Grapefruit juice, white, raw): juice of 1 grapefruit ("1 fruit yields") = 196 g

can.basis: Standard US can of beans: 15 oz (425 g), as for black beans

bunch.basis: A medium bunch of kale is about 350 g; bunch sizes vary widely (small about 200 g, large about 500 g) (cookingconverter.com; a weak source)

can.basis: Standard US can of beans: 15 oz (425 g), as for black beans

lemon.basis: USDA SR Legacy 167747 (Lemon juice, raw): juice of 1 lemon ("1 lemon yields") = 48 g
1 lemon yields 1 tbsp zest (Baking Bites); USDA SR Legacy lemon peel is 96 g per cup, so 6 g per tbsp

lime.basis: USDA SR Legacy 168156 (Lime juice, raw): juice of 1 lime ("1 lime yields") = 44 g
1 lime yields 1 to 2 tsp zest (Baking Bites), taken as 1 1/2 tsp; USDA SR Legacy lemon peel is 96 g per cup, so 2 g per tsp

orange.basis: USDA SR Legacy 169098 (Orange juice, raw): juice of 1 orange ("1 fruit yields") = 86 g
1 orange yields 1 to 1 1/2 tbsp zest (Baking Bites), taken as 1 1/4 tbsp; USDA SR Legacy orange peel is 96 g per cup, so 6 g per tbsp

bunch.basis: Parsley: '3-ounce bunch' (America's Test Kitchen, Our Handy Guide to Herb Yields)

pink grapefruit.basis: USDA SR Legacy 167774 (Grapefruit juice, pink, raw): juice of 1 grapefruit ("1 fruit yields") = 196 g

can.basis: Standard US can of beans: 15 oz (425 g), as for black beans

pepper.basis: Midpoint of '4- to 5-ounce (113- to 142-gram) poblano chiles' in America's Test Kitchen's Chiles Rellenos; those are chosen for stuffing and may run large, and grocery listings say 6-8 oz on average, so this is a rough typical weight

can.basis: Standard US can of pumpkin: 15 oz (425 g) (Libby's 100% Pure Pumpkin)

bunch.basis: A bunch of green onions, 6 to 8 medium, weighs about 3.8 ounces (105 g) (howmuchisin.com, measured at grocery stores)

large.basis: Large shallot: 1 1/2 ounces (42 g) (America's Test Kitchen, Sizing Up Shallots)

medium.basis: Medium shallot: 1 ounce (28 g); ATK recipes assume a medium shallot (America's Test Kitchen, Sizing Up Shallots)

small.basis: Small shallot: 1/2 ounce (14 g) (America's Test Kitchen, Sizing Up Shallots)

squash.basis: '1 (2 1/2-pound) spaghetti squash' (America's Test Kitchen, Spaghetti Squash Salad); other ATK recipes use 2 1/2 to 3 pounds

can.basis: Standard US can of sweetened condensed milk: 14 oz (396 g) (Eagle Brand)

bunch.basis: A bunch of thyme is about one ounce (howmuchisin.com, after several grocery stores); America's Test Kitchen lists a 3/4-ounce package

can.basis: Standard small US can of tomato paste: 6 oz (170 g) (Hunt's Tomato Paste, 6 oz)
Standard small US can of tomato sauce: 8 oz (227 g) (Hunt's Tomato Sauce, 8 oz can)
Standard US can of tuna: 5 oz, 4 oz (113 g) drained; USDA's tuna here is drained solids (StarKist Chunk Light Tuna in Water)

medium.basis: '4 yellow squashes and/or zucchini (8 ounces each)' (America's Test Kitchen, Sauteed Summer Squash)
